mainEntity.name: Why is my freezer not freezing?

acceptedAnswer.text: The common causes are a dirty condenser, a failed fan, ice blocking the evaporator because the defrost system has failed, a worn door or lid seal, a faulty thermostat or control board, or low refrigerant from a leak. A technician tests each one in turn.

mainEntity.name: Why is my freezer covered in frost or ice?

acceptedAnswer.text: Heavy frost usually means the door or lid is not sealing, the defrost heater, timer or sensor has failed in a frost-free model, or the drain is blocked. Chipping the ice off only helps for a short time. We find why it formed and fix that part.

mainEntity.name: My freezer has stopped. Should I throw out the food?

acceptedAnswer.text: Keep the door shut so the cold stays in. If the food is still hard with ice crystals, it is usually fine once the freezer is back. Food that has thawed and sat above 5°C for more than 4 hours should be thrown out and not refrozen.

mainEntity.name: Why is my freezer working but my fridge is warm?

acceptedAnswer.text: In many fridge-freezers the cold air is made in the freezer and shared with the fridge by a fan and a damper. If the freezer is cold and the fridge is warm, look for an iced-up evaporator, a failed fan or a stuck damper. Our fridge not cooling repair page covers this in more detail.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth repairing an old freezer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often yes. If the repair costs less than half the price of a similar new freezer and the freezer is under about 10 years old, repairing usually makes sense. Sealed-system faults on old freezers can tip the balance, and we will tell you plainly.
